newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian precious metals dull, subdued by politics.
newsitem.headline: Indian precious metals dull, subdued by politics.

text.p: ** Indian precious metals trade subdued as attention turned to government confidence debate.
** Gold 24 carat closed steady at 4,795 rupees per 10 grammes but off 5 rupees against today opening level of 4,800 rupees as light profit-taking at the close trimmed early gains.
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed steady at 56,100 rupees per piece after gaining 200 rupees per piece on Thursday.
** Silver (.999) closed 5 rupees lower at 7,025 rupees per kg against the previous close of 7,030 rupees amid sluggish industrial demand and higher availability of imported silver.

Indian precious metals trading was subdued on Friday as major players turned their attention to a televised government confidence debate in the run up to a vote at eight p.m. (1430 GMT) which is almost certain to end H.D. Deve Gowda's premiership.
Gold 24 carat closed unchanged at 4,795 rupees per 10 grammes, after opening five rupees higher, amid limited activity as sluggish buying matched with scattered inflow, dealers said.
"Volume remained low during the day as major players kept sidelines awaiting outcome of the no confidence motion put against United Front government in the Parliament," one broker said.
"Voting on this motion will be done in the late evening and they are awaiting the final verdict," he added.
Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed steady at 56,100 rupees per piece after gaining 200 rupees on Thursday.

Silver (.999) eased five rupees to 7,025 rupees per kg against a previous close of 7,030 rupees amid sluggish industrial enquiries and higher availability of imported silver which was put at 2,000/3,000 kg. Silver was up by 10 rupees on Thursday. (Conversion $1=35.84 rupees)
